papers_read.title_as_printed: Plasma p-tau181 as a promising non-invasive biomarker of Alzheimer's Disease pathology in Subjective Cognitive Decline and Mild Cognitive Impairment (Giacomucci et al.; Journal of the Neurological Sciences 453 (2023) 120805)

Blood biomarkers for the diagnosis of amnestic mild cognitive impairment and Alzheimer's disease: A systematic review and meta-analysis (Qu et al.; Neuroscience and Biobehavioral Reviews 128 (2021) 479-486)

what_each_reports.P-1225: Plasma p-tau181 (Simoa) in 79 memory-clinic patients (33 SCD, 32 MCI, 14 AD-d) at Careggi Hospital, Florence, sampled March 2019 to September 2022; 72 had CSF and 18 had amyloid PET. AP+ means A+ with T+ regardless of N, with T taken from CSF p-tau181 on Lumipulse. The ROC analysis excludes the AD-d group (all AP+) and merges SCD and MCI: 22 AP+ (8 SCD, 14 MCI) and 36 AP- (18 SCD, 18 MCI) in the text, one MCI patient different in Table 3. AUC 0.910, with no numeric interval printed (Fig. 4 shows a band). The Youden cut-off of 2.69 pg/mL gives accuracy 84.21%, sensitivity 86.36%, specificity 82.5%, PPV 79.17% (75.00% in the abstract) and NPV 90.32%. There are no healthy controls, and the cut-off is derived and evaluated in the same sample.
what_each_reports.P-1231: Systematic review and meta-analysis (PROSPERO CRD42020191927) of 150 studies (137 quantitative, 22 qualitative), searched to 17 May 2021. What it pools is RATIOS OF MEANS between groups: for example P-tau181 is 2.06 [1.39-3.06] for AD vs controls and 1.36 [1.20-1.54] for AD vs aMCI. Diagnostic accuracy is not pooled. Section 3.7 is a narrative systematic review of 32 eligible studies (Supplementary Table 6, not in the PDF) giving ranges, including 'P-tau 181 (AUC = 0.610-0.840; sensitivity 67-71 %; specificity 66-86 %)', described as accuracy 'in identifying AD and aMCI patients from controls'.

quantity_a: A single-study, in-sample AUC of plasma p-tau181 for BIOMARKER-DEFINED AD-pathology carriage (A+ with T+, by CSF or amyloid PET) against non-carriage, within memory-clinic SCD and MCI patients, with no controls. The reference standard's T axis is CSF p-tau181, the same analyte as the index test.
quantity_b: A RANGE of study-level AUCs, with no pooled estimate and no interval, for blood P-tau181 in separating CLINICALLY diagnosed AD and aMCI patients from controls (cognitively healthy volunteers or hospital-sampled individuals). The range comes from a 32-study systematic-review set of the literature to May 2021, across mixed assays.
incompatible_if_same: No. P-1231's 0.61 to 0.84 is the spread of individual studies' AUCs, not an interval for a common parameter, so one further study at 0.910 falls outside a spread without contradicting it. P-1225 prints no numeric AUC interval. Using its own counts (22 AP+, 36 AP-), a Hanley-McNeil standard error for an AUC of 0.910 is about 0.045, which gives an approximate 95% interval of 0.82 to 1.00. That interval reaches below the top of P-1231's range. This is my computation, not the paper's.

gates.task: mismatch: T1 (diagnostic accuracy study) vs T6 (evidence synthesis); no waiver on record.
gates.dataset_family: mismatch: a single Florence memory-clinic cohort vs the published literature to 17 May 2021. That literature cannot contain P-1225, which recruited to September 2022 and was published September 2023.
gates.validation_tier: mismatch: V1 (internal ROC, in-sample Youden cut-off) vs V2 (synthesis). The n/a rule covers only pairs of syntheses or pairs of association studies.
gates.modality_family: match: both are blood p-tau181, i.e. fluid biomarkers. The registry subtypes plasma_biomarkers and blood_biomarkers belong to one family.

endpoint_and_metric: incompatible. Both figures are AUCs in name, but the target condition and reference standard differ. P-1225 separates A+T+ carriers from non-carriers inside a patient sample with no controls; P-1231 separates clinical AD/aMCI patients from controls [q1, q2, q8]. P-1231's headline metric is a ratio of means, and its P-tau181 AUC figure is a range of study results rather than a pooled estimate [q9, q10, q11].
performance_validity: This is a performance comparison (AUC against AUC), and the flag is not triggered. P-1225's AUC of 0.910 is below 0.97 (pack: performance_suspect false). The pack flags P-1231 (performance_suspect true) because its registry Best_Metric quotes P-tau217 AUC 0.97-0.98. The flag does not apply: that figure is a synthesis quoting other studies' AUC range, not an internal-validation classifier, and the contested quantity here is P-tau181 (0.61-0.84).
independence: Independent. P-1231's search closed 17 May 2021 [q12]; P-1225 sampled March 2019 to September 2022 [q6] and was published in 2023, so it cannot be among P-1231's studies. There are no shared authors (Qu, Yu et al., Fudan/Qingdao; Giacomucci, Bessi, Nacmias et al., Florence).
grounds: P-1225's AUC measures detection of AD pathology (A+ with T+) inside SCD and MCI patients, with AD dementia excluded and no controls. P-1231's P-tau181 range measures separation of clinically diagnosed AD and aMCI patients from controls. The target condition, comparison and population all differ [q1, q2, q7, q10].

P-1225's reference standard defines T status by CSF p-tau181, the same analyte as the index test [q3, q4]. Its authors attribute their higher AUC to using the A/T(N) combination rather than amyloid positivity alone [q5], and they set it beside other target conditions with different AUCs (0.799 for amyloid-positive vs negative MCI) [q13].
P-1231 pools ratios of means, not AUCs; its 0.61-0.84 is a narrative range from 32 studies [q9, q10, q11]. There is therefore no pooled accuracy estimate or interval that P-1225 could contradict.
Three deterministic gates fail (task, dataset family, validation tier) and no waiver is on record.

record_defects: The conflict statement says 'P-1231's 150-study meta-analysis pools P-tau181 diagnostic accuracy at AUC 0.61-0.84'. The range is not pooled. P-1231 pools ratios of means [q11], and the AUC ranges come from a narrative systematic review of 32 eligible studies (Section 3.7, Supplementary Table 6) [q9].

The record says 'P-1225 reports AUC 0.910 ... in a Florence memory-clinic sample of 79 SCD/MCI/AD-dementia patients'. The ROC analysis excluded the AD-d group and merged SCD and MCI, so the AUC comes from about 58 AP-classified SCD and MCI patients, not all 79 [q2, q16].

claim_a says P-1225 supplies 'the explanation for why that figure exceeds the published range'. P-1225 explains its AUC against earlier amyloid-only SCD/MCI studies (AUC 0.814, 0.799, 0.704) [q13], not against P-1231, which it does not cite.

The record's quotes are summary-block wording, not the papers' text, although their numbers match the PDFs. Examples: 'for distinguishing aMCI and AD from controls' (the PDF has 'identifying AD and aMCI patients from controls' [q14]) and the P-1225 AUC/cut-off sentence. The claim that 'All 7 quotes verified verbatim' therefore refers to the summary blocks. The PDFs that were mapped to these papers at the time were other articles.
what_would_change_the_verdict: A genuine conflict would need a P-tau181 AUC on the same target condition in both papers, with non-overlapping intervals. Either both would have to report A+T+ vs other within SCD/MCI patients, or both would have to report clinical aMCI/AD vs healthy controls. Neither paper reports such a pair: P-1225 has no control group, and P-1231 reports no biomarker-defined target and no pooled AUC.
